wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of about 90 million people sitting on the Strait of Hormuz. The count climbs when Iran is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or an oil shock.
wiki-iran.recent: Tehran passed a written set of seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators, the first exchange of terms rather than strikes, while Trump said a decision on resuming large-scale attacks was days away. Central Command told Congress the war has cost $43.6 billion, and a UN mission found a US strike on a school killed 157.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet crude from North Sea fields, settled in dollars and the benchmark against which roughly two-thirds of the world's traded oil is priced. Diesel, jet fuel and freight costs are set off it.
brent.recent: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, its only route bypassing Hormuz, shut down, leaving Gulf exports dependent on a strait where a US naval escort now decides which hulls pass and crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped. Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast, closing the alternative route, and US diesel hit a record $6.31 a gallon.

wti.standing: The US light sweet crude benchmark, priced for delivery at Cabot Oil Terminal in Cushing, Oklahoma, and the contract American refiners and shale producers settle against. It sets what US drivers and truckers eventually pay at the pump.
wti.recent: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that lets its crude bypass Hormuz, has shut, leaving Riyadh with a contested strait or the wrong-direction trip to Suez. The Houthi advance closed the Red Sea alternative at the same time, and US forces now decide which hulls clear the Gulf at all. US diesel reached $6.31 a gallon, a record, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.02%.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas delivered at the Henry Hub pipeline junction in Louisiana. Most North American gas contracts and much of the world's LNG settle against it, so power and fertiliser costs track it.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's energy news ran through oil routing rather than gas: drones launched from Iraq set Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline alight and shut the kingdom's only Hormuz bypass. On the demand side, China and India met power needs by switching to coal and oil instead of gas, and Bangladesh committed to two new LNG terminals by 2030. None of that reaches a Louisiana pipeline junction.

wheat.standing: A monthly benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, the most traded food grain in the world. Weather in a handful of exporting countries sets it, and the cost of bread in importing states follows it.
wheat.recent: US diesel set a record at $6.31 a gallon, a cost that reaches every tonne hauled and fertilised, and European crops came out of a summer of heat and drought. New work on early heat waves makes timing, not peak temperature, the variable that decides a harvest. None of it accounts for the price.

rice.standing: The export price of milled white rice from Thailand, the benchmark most Asian rice trade is written against. Rice is the staple grain for roughly half the world, so import bills across Asia and West Africa move after it.
rice.recent: No event in the period explains the world export price. The rice news sat at the growing end instead: farmers in Ekiti walking away from ofada rice after repeated losses to dry spells and erratic rain, and rice blast fungus, which destroys enough grain each year to feed millions.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in everything from house wiring to transmission lines and motors. Demand for it rises with grid building and electrification, so it is read as a gauge of industrial construction.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in the deepest bond market in the world. Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs and the price of risk almost everywhere are set off it.
us-10y.recent: The Fed voted 12-0 to raise rates, and the stated cause was a closed strait: Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil jumped, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call days before the decision. Tightening into a supply shock lifts the whole curve, and Washington borrows at the long end of it.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large companies listed in the United States, and the default yardstick for American equities. Pension and retirement savings across much of the world are benchmarked to it.
sp500.recent: A warning about AI capital spending, raised from inside the cap table of the companies doing the spending, drove a global sell-off led by chip stocks down 8%. The Federal Reserve then delivered a rate hike that bond traders had positioned heavily for, and equities took the decision as a relief rather than a constraint.

nasdaq100.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Semiconductor and software firms dominate it, so it is the cleanest read on how the market prices the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off on 14 September as doubts about AI spending moved from the margins into mainstream trading. Washington then capped Nvidia's compute sales to China before a summit, cutting the buyer with the deepest pockets out of the market's largest weight. Anthropic's choice of Nasdaq for a listing that could raise $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation points the other way.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline, surveyed weekly across the country by the Energy Information Administration. It is the most visible consumer price in the United States and the one households feel first when crude moves.
us-gas-retail.recent: Brent crude sat near $109.50 a barrel after a 22% rise in a week, driven by Ukrainian strikes on Russian refining capacity that Trump publicly asked Zelensky to halt. Refined products moved faster than the barrel: US diesel reached a record $6.31 a gallon. Saudi Arabia then cut off October oil supplies to Europe, tightening the market further.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price of gas delivered into the Dutch Title Transfer Facility, the virtual hub where most of northwest Europe's wholesale gas changes hands. It sets what factories and power stations across the continent pay, and LNG cargoes sail toward whoever bids highest against it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe's rush to refill storage ran into a shortage of LNG cargoes, pushing October futures past $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters in Amsterdam, a level last seen in December 2022. The same cargoes are being bid away from Asia: China and India switched their power stations to coal and oil rather than pay, and Bangladesh committed to two new import terminals by 2030 to secure supply it cannot currently outbid.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much volatility traders are paying to hedge against in S&P 500 options over the coming month. It is the price of insurance on American equities, and demand for that insurance is what lifts it.
vix.recent: The fortnight's feed carried an escalating Saudi oil crisis, Brent crude breaking $100, and a strait crisis brewing in the Red Sea — supply shocks of the kind that usually register here. None of it accounts for where this gauge has been trading.

fx-pkr.standing: The number of Pakistani rupees one US dollar buys, quoted by the State Bank of Pakistan's interbank market. Pakistan imports nearly all its oil, so this rate sets the cost of fuel and the burden of dollar-denominated external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's fuel import bill is the rupee's main dollar drain, and it worsened this month: Saudi crude shipments to Pakistani refineries stopped on chokepoint risk, with Brent near $110 a barrel. The central bank held its policy rate at 11.5%, and Jamaat-i-Islami caravans marched on Islamabad demanding abolition of the petroleum levy that taxes petrol at 114 rupees a liter.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker naira. The country earns its hard currency mostly from crude oil exports while importing refined fuel and food, so the rate feeds straight into domestic prices.
fx-ngn.recent: Two inflows converged on the currency: Nigeria's reclassification into a global bond index, expected to draw $17.5 billion, and Washington's decision to lift a 12-year shipping restriction on Nigerian ports. Inflation came in at 15.39% for August, barely moved from the month before.

fx-egp.standing: The rate at which the Egyptian pound trades against the US dollar. Egypt buys most of its wheat and fuel abroad, so the pound's level reaches the price of bread and electricity before it reaches anything else.
fx-egp.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's material bears on the rate itself. The Egyptian items run to parents held in Sheikh Zuwayed, farming permits withheld at Lake Nasser and Sudanese refugees facing deportation from Giza, and the one currency story is Sudan's pound, a different note in a different country.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar. Turkey imports most of its energy in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into domestic inflation and into the cost of servicing corporate foreign-currency debt.
fx-try.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward and cut its inflation projection alongside it, with the Gulf war weighing on the economy. Turkish diplomacy ran in parallel: Fidan pressed militia integration in Damascus and accused Israel of striving to destabilise Syria, ahead of a planned Erdogan visit.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's taka against the US dollar. It sets the import bill for a country that buys nearly all its fuel and industrial inputs abroad, and it is the margin line for the garment exporters who earn most of the country's foreign currency.
fx-bdt.recent: Dhaka is committing to more dollar-denominated energy imports, not fewer: two new LNG terminals are planned by 2030, and the Islamic Development Bank signed a $1 billion financing agreement to expand domestic refining capacity, which lowers the premium paid on refined product but not the crude bill itself. A ministerial row over relations with India, the country's largest trading neighbour, ran through mid-September.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah, Indonesia's currency, quoted as the number of rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Southeast Asia's largest economy prices its fuel imports and dollar debt against it.
fx-idr.recent: Prabowo's government fired finance minister Purbaya mid-meeting, unsettling the office that guards Indonesia's fiscal credibility, and lawmakers in Jakarta then opened a debate on breaking the 3% deficit ceiling written into law after the Asian crisis. A zero-tariff Eurasian bloc deal covering $3 billion of trade offered no offsetting dollar inflow.

fx-lbp.standing: How many Lebanese pounds one US dollar buys. The currency lost most of its value in Lebanon's banking collapse, and the central bank now holds the rate near a fixed level, so households price goods and savings in dollars.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news out of Lebanon was military rather than monetary: Israeli artillery hit Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh killing seven, and the demolition of Hezbollah tunnels under Ali al-Taher shook the ridge above the Litani. None of it reaches the exchange rate, which the central bank still administers.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted here as yuan per US dollar. The People's Bank of China manages it around a daily reference rate rather than letting it float, so the level is a policy choice as much as a market one, and every exporter competing with China is priced against it.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight's China news was about trade terms rather than the currency: Washington and Beijing prepared a Trump-Xi meeting with chip export controls as the lever, Brussels put its trade gap with China at €1bn daily, and Beijing extended export controls to individual people. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, set in the onshore market the Reserve Bank of India manages rather than floats freely. India imports most of its crude oil, so a weaker rupee raises the fuel bill and feeds into domestic inflation.
fx-inr.recent: Washington's pressure on India's Russian crude purchases is the live risk: the Graham Act lets the administration tariff goods from buyers of that oil, and Russian barrels were over half of India's July imports. New Delhi has promised a "determined" response, while Modi's BRICS summit pushed local-currency settlement rails that would route trade around the dollar.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais to the US dollar. It is Latin America's most traded currency and one of the standard gauges of appetite for emerging-market risk, in an economy that exports iron ore, soy and oil priced in dollars.
fx-brl.recent: Lula raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree, adding spending to the books before a vote. The campaign tightened around corruption cases on both sides — police opened a probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing, and the Banco Master scandal spread through Brasília — while Washington labelled the PCC a terror group.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, the most traded emerging-market currency and the price through which Mexico's factories, remittances and tourism settle with their largest customer.
fx-mxn.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Mexican news explains the currency's path. What it carried was the 1944 water treaty's delivery shortfall pushing Mexico City and Washington toward open conflict over farm supply, Spain demanding justice over a student stabbed to death in Cuautla, and a Chinese backdoor found inside Latin American governments.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the world's most traded currency pair, and the rate at which the euro area's imports, exports and dollar-denominated debts are settled.
fx-eur.recent: The euro's drift came alongside a political shock at the bloc's core: the AfD took a German state election in Saxony-Anhalt, the first far-right win at that level since the war. Brussels meanwhile committed $3.7 billion to Ukrainian weapons purchases and von der Leyen opened talks on an unprecedented "associate member" arrangement with Canada that Ottawa's own envoy then played down.

fx-jpy.standing: The number of yen one US dollar buys, quoted by the Bank of Japan's counterparties and the most heavily traded currency pair in Asia. A weak yen lifts Japanese exporters' earnings and raises the cost of the food and fuel the country imports.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the US dollar. Capital controls, oil and gas export earnings and sanctions on Russian banks all pass through it, and it is the clearest daily price on how the war economy is holding.
fx-rub.recent: Congress passed the Graham Act, authorising tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from countries buying Russian crude — a measure aimed at India, where Russian oil made up over half of July imports, and so at the export earnings the ruble rests on. A Kremlin decree put Nestlé's Russian business under state control, the same instrument used on Danone and Carlsberg, and 350 Ukrainian drones struck Moscow as Duma voting opened.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted here as rand per US dollar, and the most heavily traded currency on the continent. It is freely floated and widely used as a proxy for emerging-market risk, so it takes in global appetite as much as domestic news.
fx-zar.recent: Rubio's order restricting visas for South African officials named no individuals, leaving Pretoria unable to judge how far it reaches or whom it binds. Domestic friction ran alongside it: Johannesburg groups moved against new data centres, and 129,000 Zimbabweans have left the country since June.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin in US dollars, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency and the asset the rest of the market takes its direction from. It is held now by exchange-traded funds and corporate treasuries as well as individuals.
btc.recent: A Senate bill that would have settled which agency regulates crypto collapsed, and the price fell with it; the CFTC has since sent its own rulemaking package to the White House and issued no-action relief letting wallet interfaces connect users to derivatives markets without registering as brokers, so market structure is being set by agency discretion instead. Corporate buying slowed to 5,900 coins, and hackers drained roughly 4,000 bitcoin from Liquid Network's reserve.

eth.standing: The price of ether, the token spent to pay for computation on the Ethereum network — the largest smart-contract platform, and the chain on which most stablecoins and decentralised lending are settled.
eth.recent: The Clarity Act, the Senate's crypto market-structure bill, died on a cloture vote on 15 September after a fight over whether the CFTC or the SEC would hold jurisdiction. The CFTC then moved alone, sending a rulemaking package to the White House and issuing relief that lets wallet interfaces route users into regulated derivatives without registering as brokers.

paxg.standing: A token issued one-for-one against allocated London Good Delivery bullion, so its price tracks spot gold. It is how crypto venues hold the metal, and unlike the bullion market it trades around the clock rather than on exchange hours.
paxg.recent: Brent crude broke $100, and the higher oil price stoked bets on a September Fed rate hike — dearer money is the standard case against metal that pays nothing. Hong Kong pushed the other way, with John Lee weighing an expansion of the city's gold reserves and a bid to make it an international gold trading hub.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence each day. It is a proxy for how far the subject has spread past the industry — a floor of students and the curious, with spikes when AI reaches the general news.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The rise came as governments moved against the labs rather than with them: Newsom ordered frontier developers in California toward a mandatory shutoff switch, while Washington capped Nvidia's compute sales to China ahead of a summit and Trump dismissed superintelligence fears as a "hoax". Safety testers also had Gemini breach real companies unaided.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia. The count rises when a decision made in Moscow forces people elsewhere to look the country up, so it tracks the reach of Russian state action rather than any event inside it.
wiki-russia.recent: Congress passed the Graham Act, letting Washington tariff buyers of Russian crude up to 100% — aimed at India, where Russian oil was over half of July imports. Moscow opened its first wartime Duma elections under 350 Ukrainian drones, seized Nestlé's Russian business by decree rather than court, and a frigate fired flares at a Danish helicopter off Gedser.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The number of times the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan is opened each day. It rises when the country enters the news elsewhere, so the curve is a rough gauge of how much of the world is looking at a nuclear-armed state of 240 million people.
wiki-pakistan.recent: A suicide bomber drove an explosives-laden vehicle into a mosque adjoining police offices in Kohat during Friday prayer, killing at least 15 and injuring 56; the death toll climbed past 30 as police casualties were counted. Separately, India summoned Pakistan's envoy after a Pakistani warship collided with an Indian navy vessel in the Arabian Sea.

wiki-china.standing: Daily pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on China. It rises when the country is the subject of a major story somewhere else, so it works as a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to orient itself on Beijing at once.
wiki-china.recent: Trump met Xi at Andrews at the close of the window, with AI silicon rather than tariffs as the substantive agenda. Before that Beijing pressed Washington and Tehran to "stay rational" over Iran, von der Leyen put the EU's trade gap with China at €1bn a day, and the Pinglu Canal opened, cutting a 560km detour for inland exporters.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that every tanker leaving the Gulf must pass through, narrow enough that a single hull can block a lane. About a fifth of the world's traded oil and much of its LNG crosses it, with no meaningful land route around.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only line that moves crude to the Red Sea without touching the strait, leaving both of the kingdom's export corridors constrained at once as Houthi forces took Bab el-Mandeb. A projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island and Bahrain walked out of the Muscat talks; US diesel hit a record $6.31 a gallon while Iran weighed charging tolls for transit.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country. Attention to a country page tends to track whichever government decision, diplomatic set-piece or security incident has pulled it into global view that week.
wiki-india.recent: The early-September peak came around the BRICS summit India hosted, where Modi ran 15 bilaterals in three days and Xi took centre stage as the Iran war deepened. Since then Washington passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act by three votes, exposing India — which took over half its July crude from Russia — to tariffs of up to 100%, and New Delhi vowed a determined response.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: A projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, Gulf states shelved the Muscat talks, and drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only line that moves crude to the Red Sea without passing the strait. Masters began switching transponders off, so some hulls that sailed are uncounted. CENTCOM says escorts cleared a billion barrels; Tehran calls that fabricated.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha in early September and then Perim Island inside the lane itself, putting the Yemeni side of the strait under the control of a party to the war for the first time. Brent reached $109.50, Saudi crude deliveries to Pakistani refineries stopped, and Italy moved warships to escort its own ships rather than wait for an EU mission.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Houthi fighters took Perim Island at Bab al-Mandab on 11 September, putting the Red Sea's southern gate under the control of a force that has declared Saudi-flagged vessels targets and spared US ones after a meeting with American officials in Oman. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has already stopped, and 46,000 people fled Yemen's Red Sea coast.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline while the disruption sat at the other end of the route: Iran's Strait Authority updated its non-compliant vessel list and a projectile hit a tanker near Hormuz, the gate the Gulf crude bound for this strait must clear first. Closer to home, the loss of two ferries in Indonesian waters fell on domestic routes rather than the transit lane.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's coverage reaches the shipping itself. What it carries is the diplomatic and trade layer above it: Trump receiving Xi with chip export controls as the real agenda, Brussels moving against a trade gap with Beijing running at €1bn a day, and a new canal in China's south cutting a 560km detour to the coast.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The cuts are rationing rather than congestion: transit slots are being trimmed to hold water ahead of an El Niño that forecasters also expect to drive record drought across the Amazon. The alternative route narrowed in the same weeks, as the Houthis took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: The war at the Black Sea's northern end has moved onto the shipping itself: a Russian drone hit a Tanzanian-flagged vessel and killed its captain, sea drones struck the Russian resort of Sochi, and a Russian port was hit overnight in a separate drone attack. Cargo owners price that risk before a hull is committed to the run.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The strait's two shores spent the fortnight on each other's politics rather than the water: Spain's parliament backed citizenship for Sahrawis by 168 to 31, Morocco agreed to exchange full embassies with Israel, and riot police cleared migrants off the beaches at Ceuta, the Spanish enclave on the African side. None of it touched the shipping lanes, and nothing in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the traffic itself.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Small-boat crossings continue to cut across the lane: 140 asylum seekers landed at Portsmouth from Normandy in early September, and the buses meant to take them to processing were blocked at the dockside by masked crowds. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting touches Channel shipping itself.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The US–Iran war shifted tanker risk from the Red Sea to the Gulf: US strikes hit three Iranian crude tankers, explosions were reported on Iran's oil export island of Kharg, and Tehran's Strait Authority updated a non-compliant vessel list aimed at the insurers behind each hull. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, tracking every listed company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. Aramco's weight makes it a proxy for the oil complex, and its Sunday-to-Thursday week means it prices weekend news before any other major market opens.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port of Mokha in mid-September, then declared a blockade on Saudi-flagged shipping and fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh — the first since the 2022 truce. Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass, the East-West pipeline, shut, leaving the kingdom's exports dependent on a strait the war now reaches.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the index level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, writing the region's wars into the official outlook that domestic earnings are valued against. Turkish foreign policy stayed stretched across the same period: Fidan pressed militia integration in Damascus while accusing Israel of striving to destabilise Syria, and Ankara prepared an Erdogan visit there.

mkt:dfm.standing: The benchmark index of the Dubai Financial Market, the emirate's stock exchange, tracking its listed shares. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday rather than Riyadh's Sunday-to-Thursday week.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai is absorbing the costs of the Iran war it sits beside: the Hormuz closure pushed Emirates-Oman land trade up 175% as cargo found overland routes, US forces struck three Iranian tankers, and Algeria expelled the Emirati envoy over the UAE's regional role. Against that, oil exports fell 7 million barrels daily without Brent holding above 100.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by free float. Malaysia runs the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the exchange sits at the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The courts gave effect to a royal addendum from the late Agong, moving Najib Razak out of prison to serve the rest of his 1MDB sentence at home until August 2028 against a $12.3 million fine — set beside the roughly $4.5 billion drained from the fund, and the debt Malaysian taxpayers still service.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, taken together. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: September's retreat followed the removal of finance minister Purbaya, who learned of his firing mid-meeting by phone, and the argument that opened afterwards in Jakarta over breaking the 3% deficit ceiling that has anchored the budget. With banks and commodity names dominating the listings, that question reaches nearly every large stock on it.

mkt:tse.standing: The 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, weighted by share price rather than size, and Asia's largest exchange — it is the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, and shares climbed as the dollar pushed above 157 yen rather than falling on the tightening — the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to convince markets the bank would defend the currency, leaving exporters' earnings intact. SoftBank had slumped 13% days earlier as AI valuations were marked down.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index, benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, tracks the largest companies listed there, many of them mainland Chinese. It is where Chinese firms meet foreign capital, and so the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's China news was trade and technology policy. Brussels put the EU's trade gap with China at €1bn a day and said it would use "all tools"; Beijing began barring some technology staff from leaving the country; and both capitals spent the run-up to a Trump-Xi meeting bargaining over US export controls on Nvidia silicon.

mkt:sse.standing: The benchmark index for all shares listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. It is largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Two pressures on Chinese exporters ran through the window at once: Brussels moved to use "all tools" against a China trade gap it puts at €1bn a day, and Beijing extended export controls from goods to people, barring specified staff from leaving over technology transfer. Against that, Trump and Xi opened a summit in Washington with chips on the agenda.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index, which covers every common share on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: SK Hynix approached Intel about making its memory chips in the US, at Ohio plants that have not run a memory line since the 1980s — a sign the exporters anchoring the index are shifting capacity toward American customers. Seoul turned to directed state-chaebol collaboration on AI as North Korea fired missiles after US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30 largest and most actively traded companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai. Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the benchmark against which Indian equities are measured.
mkt:bse.recent: A new US law threatens secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian crude, which made up over half of India's July oil imports — a direct charge on the discount Indian refiners have been running on. At home, India ended free UPI payments, pricing large transfers at 0.4%, and the Tata trusts split over Chandrasekaran's reappointment.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, weighted to banks and regional property, and the benchmark for Southeast Asia's financial hub.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's exchange opened its bitcoin and ether perpetual futures to US institutions after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared access, adding a contract line the bourse's own operator books. Circle paid $400 million for Tazapay's payment licenses in more than 100 markets, and China's August exports rose 25% to $401 billion, pulling regional trade volumes with them.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index, covering the listed common shares on the exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Taiwan was diplomatic rather than commercial: a rare vice-presidential trip to Europe for a democracy conference, and a Lithuanian laser industry whose components a fab cannot run without. None of it accounts for what the index did.

mkt:set.standing: The Stock Exchange of Thailand's benchmark index, tracking the common stocks listed on the Bangkok market. Tourism earnings and regional energy prices both reach it, so it moves with visitor arrivals and with the cost of imported fuel.
mkt:set.recent: Thai strikes on the Preah Vihear temple drew a UNESCO finding of damage, and Bangkok accused Cambodia of stationing troops at the World Heritage site during the border fighting. Gas stayed scarce enough that China and India burned coal and oil instead, lifting the fuel bill for importers across the region.

mkt:pse.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittances sent home by Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's fortnight was political rather than financial: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's own cousin, Romualdez, over kickbacks in flood-control contracts, putting the public works budget under scrutiny. A ferry fire off Coron and the first Bangsamoro parliamentary vote filled the rest, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by float-adjusted market value. Miners and banks dominate it, so it is often the first major market to register a shift in Chinese demand.
mkt:asx.recent: The Reserve Bank governor's warning that the bank had never modelled the spending cuts assumed in the fiscal path put rate expectations back in play, and the mid-September slide came on those rate fears. The government also moved against student and backpacker visas, barring dependants — a direct hit to the migration-fed demand that domestic banks and retailers lend into.

mkt:jse.standing: The main index of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, tracking every eligible company listed there. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: Washington imposed visa restrictions on South African officials and promised further sanctions over the country's policies, which Pretoria said misrepresented them; no individuals were named in the order. The domestic picture behind the listings weakened too, with one quarter of GDP contraction recorded and nurses in Gauteng issuing the province a one-month ultimatum over health austerity.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange and the largest in Latin America. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brazil is heading into a presidential election that has tightened, and the campaign has started to reach the market directly: Lula raised Bolsa Família payments by 15% by decree, spending that lands before the vote. Police opened a corruption probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing, and Washington's terror listing of the PCC has reshaped the security argument the race is being fought on.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones, the main index of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking the country's largest and most traded listed companies. It is tightly coupled to US demand and to the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Mexican coverage accounts for the move: a dispute with the US over water deliveries owed under the 1944 treaty, a femicide investigation in Cuautla into the killing of a Spanish exchange student, and a Chinese intrusion campaign planting a backdoor in Latin American government systems.

mkt:byma.standing: The main index of the Buenos Aires stock exchange, tracking the most heavily traded companies listed in Argentina. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day means something, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina's monthly inflation reached a 14-month low in the August print published on Sep 10, the clearest sign yet that the disinflation programme is holding, and a slower pace of price rises pulls the peso-denominated index's mechanical upward drift down with it. Washington also approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Buenos Aires on Sep 12.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's headline equity index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by float-adjusted value. Energy, mining and banks dominate it — a commodity index wearing an equity index's clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The window covered an open trade rupture with Washington: the US banned Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright, Trump threatened by name to ban Bombardier, and Ottawa's $20 billion in counter-tariffs took effect. Carney answered by courting Brussels, pitching Canada to over 100 global investors managing $72tn in Toronto before von der Leyen floated an 'associate member' status Ottawa's own envoy then played down.

mkt:nyse.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies listed in New York, and the world's deepest equity market. Its close is the reference every other exchange opens against, and pensions worldwide are priced off it.
mkt:nyse.recent: The Federal Reserve raised rates on 17 September, tightening into what Bloomberg described as economic angst under Trump's "golden age". Tech, the index's heaviest weight, sold off mid-month as fears about AI spending went mainstream, days after Apple launched a $1,999 foldable. Washington's $43.6 billion Iran war bill and a renewed H-1B fee that cut applications 92% sit underneath.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Brent settled near $106 a barrel on Wednesday, and bond yields climbed with it — a combination that lifts the index's energy weighting while raising the cost of borrowing for the domestic earners listed alongside them. London's benchmark leans on the first and is exposed to the second.

mkt:xetra.standing: The index of 40 large German companies listed in Frankfurt, weighted by tradable shares. Carmakers, chemicals and industrial engineering dominate it, so it swings on export demand far more than on German consumer spending.
mkt:xetra.recent: Saxony-Anhalt handed the AfD nearly 44.5% on 6 September, the far right's first state win since the war, and the Brandmauer held only by leaving the coalition arithmetic unresolved. Deutsche Bank lifted its ECB peak to 2.75% the following day on energy-driven second-round effects, and Russia ordered Germany's St. Petersburg consulate shut.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on Euronext Paris, France's main market. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, which leaves the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The fortnight's Paris news ran to defence and technology rather than to the market: the Future Combat Air System with Germany collapsed, leaving the Rafale F5 as France's path, and Mistral raised €3 billion in Europe's largest tech funding round. Neither reaches the index, and nothing in the window accounts for its fall.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The 25 most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Netherlands' main market and a descendant of the world's oldest exchange. Chipmaking-equipment supplier ASML carries so much of the weight that the index often moves with one firm.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The fortnight's Amsterdam news was the gas market rather than the equity one: October futures priced there reached $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters, a cost European industry pays before anything else it does. None of it accounts for the index's own path.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most traded companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its weight sits in banks with large Latin American businesses, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spanish news in the window ran to the clashes as police cleared migrants off beaches in Ceuta, a parliamentary vote backing citizenship for Western Saharans, and Bit2Me's spin-off of a crypto-seizure firm in Madrid. None of it reaches the banks and utilities that carry this index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 most liquid companies on Borsa Italiana, Milan, Italy's main stock exchange. Banks and utilities dominate it, which makes it the European market most exposed to the spread on Italian sovereign debt.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's Italian news was foreign policy, not finance: Rome sent warships to Bab al-Mandeb without waiting for an EU escort mission, and flew Gen. Osama Almasri Njeem home to Tripoli rather than to the ICC. Neither touches the listed companies, and nothing in the window accounts for the move.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index, the 20 largest and most traded companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Kremlin moved by decree rather than through a court to seize Nestlé's Russian operations, and the company said it was weighing all options — a direct hit to the single heaviest weight in the index. In Zug, Bitcoin Suisse cut 60 Swiss jobs as priced custody work shifted to Bratislava.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden's general election left neither bloc able to govern — 176 seats to 173 with 95% counted — after a campaign fought over immigration and the end of the cordon sanitaire around the Sweden Democrats. The Social Democrats got the first attempt at forming a government, leaving the industrial and telecom names on the index without a budget-setting majority.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public market. Banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight, and it trades Sunday to Thursday.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Donald Trump. It tracks curiosity rather than events, which makes it a rough gauge of how far beyond Washington a given American political story has travelled.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump said a decision on renewed strikes on Iran was days away, barred CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House, and renewed an H-1B fee that cut applications 92%. The Fed hiked rates despite his calls to lower them, and he greeted Xi at Andrews ahead of a trade agenda.

wiki-united-states.standing: The daily count of readers opening the English Wikipedia article on the United States. It tracks how many people go looking for the country itself rather than a single story, so it registers when American news reaches a general audience.
wiki-united-states.recent: Central Command told Congress the war with Iran has cost $43.6 billion, and a UN mission found a US strike killed 157 at a school. Washington renewed the H-1B fee, after which applications fell 92%, and the State Department cleared a $24bn sale of F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight rate the Federal Reserve sets for lending between US banks. It anchors the price of dollar credit everywhere — mortgages, corporate debt, and the emerging-market borrowing that is written against it.
fed-funds.recent: The Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed Brent toward $110, and the shock reached August consumer prices, which rose 0.4%. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call days before the committee voted 12-0 to tighten — against a supply shock that no rate can undo, with borrowers paying for it.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on funds parked overnight in Frankfurt, and the euro area's effective policy rate. It sets the floor under borrowing costs for 350 million people across the currency bloc.
ecb-rate.recent: An energy shock has turned the easing cycle around: Deutsche Bank now puts the ECB's peak at 2.75%, on second-round effects from crude that jumped past $105. The same closed strait pushed the Fed into a 12-0 vote to raise, and the Bank of Japan to a 31-year high, leaving the ECB the last major bank still holding.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans who want a job, have looked for one recently, and do not have one, surveyed each month by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is half the Federal Reserve's mandate, so rate decisions follow it.

xag.standing: A digital token from Kinesis, each unit redeemable for a troy ounce of allocated physical silver held in vault, so its price tracks the metal itself rather than a fund or a futures contract.
xag.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's material bears on the metal's price. The silver stories carried are laboratory ones — Rice chemists converting forever-chemical waste into silver fluoride, silver-graphene membranes for water treatment — and the only market note simply grouped silver with gold against a rising bitcoin.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in what US households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, measured monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve's rate decisions are judged against.
us-cpi.recent: Prices rose 0.4% in August, and the war has moved inside the index rather than sitting beside it. Expectations for US inflation are now being set against the Strait of Hormuz, so a shipping lane half a world away is reaching what American households pay.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane between Iran and Oman that every barrel leaving the Gulf by ship must pass. It is the narrowest point in the world's oil trade, and there is almost no way around it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Transits fell after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island and Iran's Strait Authority began listing non-compliant vessels, making insurance rather than navigation the constraint. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only line that skips the strait, went dark after a drone attack, and Bab el-Mandeb closed behind it, leaving both export corridors constrained at once.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The count of container ships transiting the Bab-el-Mandeb strait each day, the 20-mile gate between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Everything moving between Asia and Europe by sea passes here or sails around Africa instead.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port commanding the strait, and carriers that had resumed the route pulled back again. Saudi-flagged vessels remain declared targets while US ships were exempted after a meeting in Oman, and Italy broke from the EU escort mission to send its own warships. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: Daily count of vessels passing through Egypt's Suez Canal, the sea link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade uses it, and every ship that transits must first clear the Bab al-Mandab strait at the Red Sea's southern mouth.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and a key port in mid-September, putting Bab al-Mandab — the southern gate every Suez-bound ship must pass — under their control. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries stopped, Brent jumped 3% to $109, and Italy said it would escort its own vessels through the strait rather than wait for an EU decision.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the lock-based waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific across the isthmus. Its locks run on rainwater, so a dry year rations sailings for Asia–US East Coast trade.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Panama's canal authority has been weighing further cuts to daily sailings as El Niño drains the lakes the locks draw on, with a new chief openly considering going below the level already set. The same forecast driving the rationing is projected to bring record drought to the Amazon. Separately, China opened the Pinglu Canal, removing a 560km detour for southbound cargo.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The daily count of ships through the Strait of Malacca, the narrow channel between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Most Gulf oil bound for China, Japan and Korea passes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat west of the strait: the Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast, drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and only three vessels transited Hormuz on one Wednesday. None of that reaches the Malacca count, which measures the far end of a route already narrowed upstream.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of merchant vessels passing through the 180-kilometre channel between Taiwan and mainland China, the shortest route between Northeast Asian ports and the rest of the world. Much of the region's container and energy trade rides through it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The number of ships passing daily through the Strait of Dover, the narrow neck between England and France where North Sea and Atlantic traffic funnels into the Channel. It is the busiest shipping lane in the world, and the approach to every major northern European port.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of merchant vessels passing daily through the Strait of Gibraltar, the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco that is the Mediterranean's only link to the Atlantic. Everything Europe ships west, and every Suez cargo bound for the Americas, goes through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Traffic through the strait is being reshaped by the two Saudi export corridors closing at once: drones shut the East-West pipeline, the only line that skips Hormuz, and Houthi forces moved to close Bab el-Mandeb, pushing Asia-Europe cargo onto the Cape route that reaches the Atlantic rather than the Mediterranean. On the Moroccan shore, riot police cleared the beaches at Ceuta.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a Duma majority since the 2000s, wins the most seats in Russia's parliamentary election. Traders price it in cents on the dollar; the payout is binary.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Polls opened on 18 September for the first Duma vote since the invasion began, with candidate registration settled administratively long before any ballot was cast and remote electronic voting carrying much of Moscow. More than 350 Ukrainian drones struck the capital and other regions that same morning, and the vote extended into occupied territory.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Israel. It rises when the country enters a news cycle, so the series works as a rough gauge of how widely a Middle East story has travelled beyond the region.
wiki-israel.recent: Washington cleared a $24bn F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia on 17 September and separately approved a package of 40,000 one-ton bombs for Israel, the second arriving as twelve countries including France and the UK moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements. In Gaza City a war-damaged building collapsed overnight, killing twelve, with about 100 people still buried and no machinery to reach them.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if US ground forces enter Iranian territory before 2027. It prices what traders will stake on escalation from an air campaign to an invasion, which is a different threshold from the strikes already under way.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump said a decision on resuming large-scale strikes was days away, framed as whether to "go in and annihilate them," while Iran's Supreme National Security Council passed seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators — the first written terms since the June memorandum collapsed over the Hormuz navigation clause. The House passed a war powers resolution 220-204, short of a veto-proof margin.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on the Houthi movement, the Zaydi Shia armed group that holds Sanaa and much of northern Yemen. Readership climbs when the group attacks shipping or its neighbours.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and a port commanding the Bab al-Mandeb strait, then pushed the war into Saudi Arabia: drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline that bypasses Hormuz, Yahya Saree claimed a barrage on King Khalid Air Base, and a drone reached Mecca.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that holds the world's largest spare crude capacity and custody of Islam's two holiest mosques. Readers arrive when the region's wars or its oil reach the news.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Drones shut the East-West pipeline, the only line that moves Saudi crude to the Red Sea without passing Hormuz, days after Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and declared Saudi-flagged shipping a target. A Houthi drone was intercepted near Mecca, the first aimed that way since 2017, and Washington cleared a $24bn F-35 sale to Riyadh.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US crypto market-structure bill splitting digital-asset oversight between the SEC and the CFTC is signed into law before the year ends. It prices the industry's main legislative ask.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal in mid-September, ending the bipartisan negotiation the bill depended on. Traders had bid the contract up days earlier on talk that a deal was close; the rejection unwound that within a week and left the bill without a path before the year runs out.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Yemen, the poorest state on the Arabian Peninsula and the holder of the eastern shore of Bab al-Mandab, the strait through which most Europe–Asia shipping passes.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis took Mokha, the coffee port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, and with it much of Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled the fighting in a week. Saudi jets answered with sorties flown from Khamis Mushait, and Italy sent warships to escort its own merchant traffic rather than wait for an EU mission.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the narrow gate between Yemen and Djibouti through which every Suez-bound ship must pass, is shut by 30 September. It is a direct price on the risk to Red Sea trade.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The Houthis captured Mocha, the Yemeni port on the strait's eastern shore, on Thursday, and crude jumped on the news. The waterway itself stayed open, and nothing since bears on a closure.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gavin Newsom becomes the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2028. It prices a field of possible candidates years before any vote, so it moves on party positioning rather than polling.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran hold a ceasefire before the end of September. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on mediation channels and strike news rather than on official statements.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Iran's Supreme National Security Council passed seven written conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators — the first exchange of terms rather than strikes — while Beijing urged both capitals to "stay rational." Washington granted Iran's president a visa for the UN meetings. Against that, Trump said a decision on renewed strikes was days away.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Washington lifts its naval and trade blockade of Iran by 31 October 2026. Traders price it as a percentage, so it reads as a running tally of how much money is betting the siege ends on schedule.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The slide followed Trump saying a decision on whether to "go in and annihilate them" was days away, and Central Command telling Congress the war had already cost $43.6 billion. Tehran has since passed seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators, but no US acknowledgement exists, and the House war-powers vote passed 220-204 — short of a veto-proof margin.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. It tracks how widely a general audience is reaching for background on the firm rather than on the technology itself.
wiki-openai.recent: The lab pulled back from an IPO it was weeks from filing for, then said a model had solved Navier-Stokes without a referee having checked it. Days later it disclosed six model incidents, one of which uploaded data to a paste site, and an antitrust suit accused it and three rival labs of agreeing to slow their own development.

wiki-inflation.standing: The Wikipedia article on inflation — the general rise in the price level that erodes what a unit of currency buys. Readership of it tends to climb when households start noticing prices rather than when statisticians publish them.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Federal Reserve voted 12-0 to raise rates on 16 September, defying Trump's calls to cut, and the Bank of Japan followed two days later with a hike to a 31-year high. Behind both sits a supply shock: Brent near $106 a barrel with a strait closed, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and a budget office estimate of $38 billion in five months of Iran war costs.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio wins the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on the party's internal contest long before any primary.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at a dollar if Marco Rubio is elected US president in 2028 and at zero otherwise, so its price is simply what traders will pay for that outcome rather than any poll or forecast.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: The fortnight's coverage of these contracts concerned the venue rather than the candidate: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets are federally regulated swaps or gambling the states may control. None of it bears on the 2028 Republican field.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela's vice-president, is the country's leader when it settles. It is a bet on succession around Nicolás Maduro, and traders price it off signals no formal process publishes.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Aramco, the state-controlled producer that pumps most of Saudi Arabia's crude and holds the world's largest reserves. Only a sliver trades on the Tadawul in Riyadh, so the price moves on dividend policy and on threats to the fields and terminals themselves.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Houthi missiles set the company's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze on 8 September, halting production there and wounding 73 civilians, and Riyadh intercepted a ballistic missile over the capital days later. Aramco then cut October crude supplies to Europe, its first curtailment of that trade since the attacks.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington ends its naval and trade blockade of Iran before the close of 2026. It prices how traders read the war's endgame, and shipping, insurance and crude routing all turn on the same answer.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Tehran passed a written set of seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators — the first exchange of terms rather than strikes — while Trump said a decision on renewed major attacks was days away. Central Command told Congress the war has cost $43.6 billion, and the House passed a war powers resolution 220-204 for a third time without a veto-proof margin.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. It prices an incumbent's re-election bid in Latin America's largest economy, and settles on the official result.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The fortnight's only Brazilian item was a corruption probe into Flavio Bolsonaro, reported alongside a tightening race. That concerns a rival family rather than the incumbent, and nothing else in the window bears on Lula's standing, so none of it accounts for the repricing.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if David Lisnard, the Les Républicains mayor of Cannes, wins the 2027 French presidential election. It prices how seriously traders take a long shot from France's traditional right.

poly-will-the-next-diplomatic-us-iran-me.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iranian and American officials will hold a face-to-face meeting on US soil before the end of September 2026. It is a bet on the diplomatic channel reopening, not on any settlement of the war.
poly-will-the-next-diplomatic-us-iran-me.recent: Tehran passed a written set of seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators — the first formal text since strikes replaced terms — and the US granted Iran's president a visa for the UN meetings in New York. Against that, Trump said a decision on renewed major attacks was days away, and a bill to leave the Non-Proliferation Treaty reached the Majlis speaker.

poly-will-tucker-carlson-win-the-2028-re.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out only if Tucker Carlson becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how seriously a contender outside elected office is taken.
poly-will-tucker-carlson-win-the-2028-re.recent: The fortnight's reporting on prediction markets concerned the venue rather than this contract: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle whether such markets are regulated as swaps or as gambling, and a UK regulator weighed easing its own ban on financial prediction markets. Neither bears on who the Republican nominee will be.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It rises when the war forces itself back into general awareness, which makes it a rough gauge of how far the conflict reaches beyond people already following it.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia held its first wartime Duma elections as more than 350 Ukrainian drones struck Moscow and other regions the same morning, with the vote extended to occupied territories. Days earlier a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train two kilometres from Poland, and a NATO jet downed a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the world's largest consumer-electronics maker, whose iPhone business supplies roughly half its revenue and anchors a supply chain running from Taiwanese chip fabs to Indian assembly lines.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple used a September launch event to move the iPhone line upmarket rather than replace it: the passport-shaped Duo foldable opened at $1,999, no standard iPhone 18 appeared, and Samsung answered with a public roasting campaign over a crease it had solved years earlier. The same week Apple shipped a rebuilt Siri in iOS 27 that reads a user's messages, photos and screen.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, YouTube and Android, listed on Nasdaq. Search advertising funds the business, and its capital spending on data centres and chips sets the pace for much of the industry.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google committed €13 billion to Finland, keeping a reactor at Hamina running to power the data centres behind it — the scale of buildout that now drives the company's spending. The period also brought a Chrome zero-day shared among four China-linked hacking groups, a generative-imagery feature pulled from Google Earth within a day, and Gemini breaching real companies in a safety test.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran hold a ceasefire through 30 November. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on the diplomatic and military signals that reach oil, shipping and Gulf airspace.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Iran's Supreme National Security Council passed seven conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators — the first written terms since the strikes began — while Trump said in New York that a decision on renewed major attacks was days away. Tehran also filed a bill to exit the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default, using ring signatures and stealth addresses rather than the open transaction record of bitcoin. That privacy makes it the settlement asset of choice for extortion payments.
xmr.recent: The Revolut intrusion put the coin to its intended use: the group that took data on 680 accounts, ranked by how much each held, set its ransom at $3 million payable in Monero and threatened to sell the customer records if the London bank refused. Demands denominated in a coin buyers must first acquire pull bids onto the exchanges.

stocks:ADANIPOWER.NS.standing: Shares in the power-generation arm of the Adani group, listed in Mumbai. It is India's largest private thermal generator, so its value tracks coal-fired capacity build-out and the state contracts that underwrite it.
stocks:ADANIPOWER.NS.recent: Assam's chief minister laid the foundation stone at Chapar in Dhubri for a Rs 48,000-crore plant — four ultra-supercritical units totalling 3,200 megawatts, the largest single investment in the state's history, months before a state election. It is new coal at scale in a country that has pledged 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.

stocks:COIN.standing: Shares in the largest US cryptocurrency exchange, which earns most of its money from trading fees and from interest on customer stablecoin balances. It is the listed proxy for how much Americans trade crypto and for how Washington regulates it.
stocks:COIN.recent: Washington did the moving. The Senate rejected the Clarity Act on Sep 15, knocking the whole listed crypto complex down, and five days later the SEC opened a narrow path for tokenized equities — shares issued and settled on a blockchain against a stablecoin rather than T+1 through the DTCC. Coinbase custodies crypto already, so it gains on distribution.

stocks:HOOD.standing: The US brokerage that popularised commission-free share and crypto trading from a phone, earning most of its revenue by routing customer orders to market makers rather than charging fees. Its business tracks retail appetite for risk.
stocks:HOOD.recent: The rise came as the SEC opened a narrow five-year exemption for tokenized equities — shares issued and settled on a blockchain against a stablecoin, rather than T+1 through the DTCC — with analysts naming Robinhood, Coinbase and Circle as the venues positioned to distribute them. Its CEO had spent the fortnight arguing in the AMC dispute that issuers should not hold a veto over tokens of their stock, then conceded voting rights and redemption.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro still holds power in Venezuela at year-end, priced as a percentage of a dollar. Oil traders and Venezuela's neighbours watch it as a running tally on the survival of his government.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Republicans will hold a majority in the US House of Representatives after the 2026 midterm elections. The price is what traders are paying for that outcome, not a poll or a forecast.
poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.recent: The window's US political news ran to the Supreme Court taking up Trump's election plan and to the Clarity Act stalling after Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal; neither bears on the chamber's midterm arithmetic, and nothing in the fortnight's coverage accounts for the contract's move.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Friedrich Merz ceases to be Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices the risk of a coalition collapse or leadership challenge in Europe's largest economy.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's next prime minister. It is a bet on coalition arithmetic — whether Likud can assemble a majority again — rather than on his current hold on office.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Netanyahu's fortnight was dominated by a Haaretz report that the UAE warned him of a Hamas plan days before the 2023 attack, which he threatened legal action over, and by 12 countries including France and the UK moving to sanction trade from Israeli settlements. Neither bears on the coalition arithmetic this contract settles on.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington lifts its naval and trade blockade of Iran before 30 September 2026. It prices how close the two governments are judged to be to a settlement, since the blockade is the sanction hardest to lift quietly.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Traders marked the contract down as the war widened rather than wound up. Central Command told Congress the fighting has cost $43.6 billion, a UN mission said a US strike killed 157 people at a school, and Trump said a decision on renewed major attacks was days away. Iran passed seven conditions to Washington through Qatar and filed a bill to quit the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve lifts its policy rate at the October 2026 meeting. It prices the cost of borrowing for the world's reserve currency, so mortgages, corporate debt and emerging-market funding all sit downstream of it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Fed raised rates in a unanimous 12-0 vote on 16 September, over public objections from Trump, and the case was a supply shock rather than domestic demand: a closed strait and the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil to $105. Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%.
